text:
harper (People Ops): FYI - we rolled back the scorecard template v3 -> v2 for Backend SWE this morning and now some panels show responses that don't map to the older fields. Noticed this on P-4456 and P-4490.
liam (Recruiting Ops): saw that too. Interviewers completed feedback against v3 last week; rolling back created mismatch because field slugs changed (`system-design` -> `design_architecture`). Candidates' feedback present but sections missing on v2.
tess (Interview Training): why was v3 rolled back? I thought v3 was the approved rubric after calibration.
noah (Eng - Integrations): ops rolled it back due to a bug in the front-end that caused questions to render twice for some users. The rollback was quick but we didn't run a migration to map v3 responses to v2 field slugs. That is causing orphaned answers.
harper (People Ops): concrete impact: hiring managers opening panels see blank sections even though interviewers left notes; some teams may miss feedback before decisions. We need an emergency plan to surface and migrate responses.
nats-webhook-bot: deploy event: rollback scorecard v3 -> v2 triggered by ops at 2026-06-08T09:14:02Z (evt id rb-309)
scorecard-service-bot: audit note: 7 panels with unmapped responses detected (query id audit-307)
liam (Recruiting Ops): can we programmatically remap obvious slug changes? e.g., copy `system-design` responses to `design_architecture` in v2 or vice-versa depending on direction. Some fields are renamed but semantically identical.
noah (Eng - Integrations): yes, we can write a migration script with a mapping table. Need a canonical mapping from product/trainers. Also need to mark migrated responses so we can revert if needed. I'll queue a one-off job but want signoff from Training/Product on mappings.
tess (Interview Training): here's initial mapping I can confirm:
```
{"system-design": "design_architecture", "api-design": "api_quality", "testing": "test_strategy"}
```
These three cover ~80% of changes. For others we need manual review.
liam (Recruiting Ops): please include a safety check: only migrate responses where the source field on v3 is non-empty and the destination field on v2 is empty, to avoid overwriting.
noah (Eng - Integrations): agree. Migration plan:
- create mapping table (from tess)
- run dry-run report (no writes) listing panels that would change (job dryrun-412)
- post results to this channel for review
- if OK, run migration with write and attach migration log and revert plan (job mig-413)
ETA for dry-run: 60m. Full migration ETA after review: 3h.
harper (People Ops): please also tag hiring owners in the dry-run report so they can preview. We need to prioritize panels with upcoming decisions first.
scorecard-service-bot: dry-run-412 queued at 2026-06-08T10:02:30Z
liam (Recruiting Ops): also, add a temporary UI banner for affected panels: "This panel was created against an incompatible rubric version. Some answers may be hidden; hiring owners please review." Can product prod-bot help with banner?
noah (Eng - Integrations): quick banner deployed via admin flag: banner active on panels with audit-307 tag.
tess (Interview Training): I'll prepare an internal note for interviewers explaining what happened and how we migrated answers so they aren't surprised.
harper (People Ops): thanks. After migration, we should run a calibration audit on a sample of migrated panels to confirm mapping fidelity.
noah (Eng - Integrations): dry-run results posted: 7 panels would be migrated; 3 prioritized with decisions due today. Posting CSV to the hiring owners channel and sending DMs.
liam (Recruiting Ops): I got the CSV and confirm proceed for the 3 urgent panels.
noah (Eng - Integrations): migration mig-413 ran at 2026-06-08T12:10:05Z. All targeted fields copied with audit markers. Migration log: mig-413-log-20260608 (attached).
scorecard-service-bot: migration summary: 7 panels processed, 12 field mappings applied, no overwrites (safety check passed).
harper (People Ops): closing loop for now. Great cross-team response. We'll follow up with a postmortem and add a runbook step to avoid rollbacks without migrations in the future. :white_check_mark:
